# Denylist TEMPLATE — safe to commit, because it names nothing real.
#
# Copy it, fill it in, and keep the copy out of git:
#
#   cp .github/denylist.example.txt .githooks/denylist.local.txt
#
# .gitignore already refuses to track denylist.local.txt. That is the whole
# point: a committed denylist is a public, searchable index of exactly which
# words someone considers sensitive, which is worse than having no denylist.
#
# For CI, put the same content in a repo secret named GUARD_DENYLIST:
#   gh secret set GUARD_DENYLIST < .githooks/denylist.local.txt
#
# Matching is case-insensitive fixed-string, one term per line. No regex, no
# escaping. Lines starting with # are ignored.
#
# Keep terms specific enough not to fire constantly. "Acme" is a good entry;
# "data" is not — a rule that cries wolf gets bypassed, and a bypassed rule
# protects nothing.

# ── Employers, past and present ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# The company name itself is usually fine to say publicly (it is on your
# résumé). What you are guarding is the layer beneath it: internal system
# names, service names, team names, repo names, product codenames.
#
# YourEmployerInternalPlatformName
# some-internal-service
# ProjectCodename

# ── Clients and counterparties ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Often the most contractually sensitive category. Anyone whose name appears in
# an MSA or NDA you have signed.
#
# BigClientCo
# CLIENT-1234

# ── Internal infrastructure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Hostnames, bastion names, VPC/account identifiers, internal domains, database
# names, queue names, S3 buckets.
#
# prod-db-primary
# 10.0.
# your-internal-domain.net
# arn:aws:iam::123456789012

# ── Identifiers that leak structure ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Ticket prefixes, internal URLs, wiki spaces.
#
# JIRA-PROJ-
# confluence.yourcompany
# yourcompany.slack.com

# ── People ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Colleagues who have not consented to appearing in your public commit history.
#
# (names go in the local copy, obviously, not here)
